hypothesis: Reuse the normal executable path to retire the closed native-return tree without losing its borrowed-input/no-workspace benefit.
findings: Ordinary functions already defer invocation contexts and bind into final shared local/operand arrays.
The direct native call borrows the caller operand slice before binding; its guard tree precedes effects.
The existing ordinary work state requires an array-backed locals/operand workspace even when no invocation context is created.
Native evaluation shares underlying primitives and shape facts; its separate tree avoids workspace construction/binding and permits entry proof before admission.
Blindly removing that tree reverses the measured allocation benefit; retaining its input behavior in the normal engine requires a broader operand-storage change.

The prior B69 arena also removed call allocations and still regressed complete CSV/text5.0to6.8%; the control-record trial retained allocation and regressed. These are cautionary evidence, not permanent vetoes.
decision: No bounded native-return consolidation prototype selected. Preserve measured optimization and correct guards. A future shared storage redesign must demonstrate benefit through complete scripts, retain caller/async borrows and remove displaced machinery. This phase stops at the explicit storage/guard tradeoff, not another CPU capture.
